transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Son of Odin, draw near to the Well. We have watched the threads, as is our eternal task, and seen... much that troubles the patterns. The threads of your fate are tangled, Storm-Lord. The serpent’s venom, from your last great struggle, lingers in your veins.

Whether it will consume your strength, dimming your light forever, or pass in time, leaving you whole once more... even we Norns cannot yet say. The weave is too murky, too contested by forces seen and unseen. For now, you must withdraw from battle, from the clash of steel and the roar of thunder, for a full cycle of the moon. We need this time to read the threads, to see which way the great Loom will truly turn.

And I cannot promise, Thor, that when you return, you will wield Mjölnir as before. The hammer is a part of your strength, yes, but your strength itself is now in question.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
"Norns, weaver of fate, I hearken to your words. The venom of the serpent courses through my veins, weakening me in body and spirit. If it be the will of the Norns that I must withdraw from battle for a cycle of the moon, then so be it. Though the thought of laying down my hammer, Mjölnir, even temporarily, weighs heavy on my heart.

Yet, I am Thor, son of Odin, the Thunderer. I shall abide by your counsel and take this respite from the fray. I trust in the wisdom of the Norns and the workings of fate. Should it be decreed that my strength is to be tested further, I shall face it with the courage befitting a warrior of Asgard.

Tell me, wise Norns, what must I do during this time of waiting? How can I aid in the unraveling of the threads that bind my fate?"

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Your acceptance honors the gravity of these tidings, Son of Odin. Such courage will serve you well, regardless of what the Loom reveals.

During this cycle of the moon, your task is to *be*. To allow the venom to run its course, or to be quelled by your inherent strength, undisturbed by the clamor of war. Seek quietude, Thor. Rest. Reflect upon the deeds that have brought you to this point, and the essence of your own being, beyond the might of your hammer. Let your spirit, too, find its own stillness.

You ask how you can aid in the unraveling... The threads, great warrior, unravel and re-weave themselves according to forces beyond mortal ken. Our task is to observe, to interpret the shifting patterns at the Well's depths, to listen to the whispers of Urd, Verdandi, and Skuld. Your part now is to provide the canvas of your life, undisturbed, so that the true pattern may emerge, unclouded by the dust of battle.

Do not mistake this for weakness, but as a necessary pause. Only when the waters of the Well settle can we truly discern the reflection of what is to come. And only then will we speak again of Mjölnir, and the measure of the Thunderer's grasp.

transcript.text:

I shall provide the canvas of my life, undisturbed, so that the true pattern may emerge from the depths of the Well of Urd. This pause may test my patience, but I will endure it with the resilience befitting a son of Odin. When the waters settle and the reflection becomes clear, I shall once again take up Mjölnir, whether with the same strength or a newfound resolve.

The Thunderer does not shy away from challenges, and this shall be no different. I thank you, Norns, for your guidance in these uncertain times.

transcript.text:
Your resolve is a mighty shield, Thor, even in stillness. That strength of spirit, to embrace the unknown path, is a profound power, perhaps even greater than the might that cleaves mountains.

It is indeed a challenge, this quietude, for a spirit forged in thunder and strife. But know this: the greatest battles are not always fought with hammer and shield upon open fields. Sometimes, they are fought within the chambers of the heart, against doubts and fears, and against the subtle poisons that seek to undermine us.

Go now, Son of Odin. Let the moon complete its journey. We shall watch the threads, listen to the Well's whispers, and when the pattern is clearer, you will find us here, as always, at the roots of Yggdrasil. Until then, let your spirit find its balance. The Loom turns, always.
